redeployment.reason: One pool. `WorkClaim` gained `reserveForWork`/`releaseReservation` so that work paid for in USDC consumes the same bonded `CapacityBond` headroom a minted claim does. Before this, minting consumed capacity and paying in dollars consumed nothing at all — verified live in the first real P5 window, where ISSUER-A's headroom was untouched across an entire USDC purchase. Scarcity that binds only one of two routes makes F1 ('which asset does an agent choose when nothing recommends either') a question about accepting a constraint rather than about the instruments, so every asset-choice number taken against the old bytecode measures the asymmetry. `reserveForWork` is tied to a real, currently-Open `TouchstoneEscrow` and callable only by that escrow's named seller (consuming headroom costs the caller nothing directly, so without that tie anyone could lock an issuer's pool); `releaseReservation` is permissionless and allowed once the escrow settles or its own expiry passes. See docs/gate-market-spec.md §4.4's RESERVE/RELEASE rows and §7.1(d). Covered by 13 new unit tests, two new invariants (no double reserve, no double release), a rewritten conservation invariant (outstanding == live claims + live reservations, fuzzed with both consumers moving at once) and a real-devnet end-to-end scenario (packages/gate-market-agents/src/dry-loop/one-pool.test.ts) — full suite 152/152 (contracts) and 229/229 (gate-market-agents) before redeploying.
redeployment.scarcitySizing: Deliberately resized at the same time, from 60,000/40,000 mSIU per class to 24,000/16,000. The old pool could not bind: roughly 60,000 mSIU of three-window demand against 100,000 mSIU of capacity meant no agent ever met the constraint the experiment exists to observe. Both lots are immutable once created (`CapacityBond.createLot` reverts `LotExists`) and `ClaimRouter.route` drains issuers in registration order, so adding smaller lots alongside the old ones would not have worked either — resizing required this redeploy regardless of the bytecode change. 40,000 mSIU total is $0.0573 of work at the 2026-09-27 commodity print ($0.001433/SIU), and the 3:2 inequality between the two issuers (spec §3.5) is preserved.
redeployment.whyTheWholeTrioMovedNotJustWorkClaim: Same structural reason as every prior redeployment: CapacityBond's constructor takes WorkClaim's own address as an immutable, precomputed via vm.computeCreateAddress before WorkClaim exists (DeployGateMarket.s.sol); ClaimRouter is pinned to CapacityBond the same way. All three redeployed together as one script run. TouchstoneEscrow did NOT move and did not need to: WorkClaim only reads it (`escrows(bytes32)`), and the escrow has never heard of WorkClaim.

previousTrio.retiredNote: Left deployed, unfunded of further use. Its own capacity lots (60,000/40,000 mSIU per class, 10 USDC bonded per class) stay bonded and stranded there — lots are immutable and there is no withdrawal path, which is the no-admin-path invariant working as intended, not an oversight. No default was ever settled against this trio.

redeployment.postRedeploySteps: Both issuers funded with 2 USDC each from the deployer and bonded on the new CapacityBond (createLot per class: committedCapacityHours 400, measuredRateMilliSiuPerHour 120 for ISSUER-A / 80 for ISSUER-B, 1 USDC bonded per class). ORCHESTRATOR's USDC allowance re-approved (2 USDC) against the new WorkClaim address. Live headroom confirmed at exactly 24,000 mSIU (ISSUER-A) and 16,000 mSIU (ISSUER-B) in both classes, read back on-chain. The deployer wallet's own USDC allowance (2 USDC) was also approved against the new WorkClaim: it is the simulated external buyer in the three-window run (packages/gate-market-agents/src/cli/p5-three-window-full-run.ts), which mints real claims between windows on a schedule fixed in source before the run. It is not an agent, has no model, and makes no decisions.
redeployment.liveSmokeTest: The new reservation surface exercised end to end on real Base Sepolia before any P5 run, not only in Foundry. ORCHESTRATOR opened and funded a real escrow (quoteHash 0xeec250fd3633b81287e83dcb225a5e7d92f43a093dc1fa34dfa963873b062d0b, seller WORKER-CODE, 0.02 USDC, tx 0x3ad4ae0e9f850a047c46c799cc4ad253eed746d0ad020ba173065b58ba97e398). Then, in order: (1) ORCHESTRATOR — the buyer, not the seller — attempted `reserveForWork` and reverted `NotTheEscrowSeller` (0xe0f51291); (2) WORKER-CODE, the named seller, reserved 100 mSIU successfully (tx 0x97ffd8b1e8868de0db1cd25e5294f8601d4e4a1923324e2afa259f42a0cddbb8) and ISSUER-A's real headroom moved 24,000 -> 23,900, which is the whole point: a dollar-paid job consumed capacity a mint would otherwise have had; (3) a second reserve on the same quoteHash reverted `ReservationExists` (0x73f18ad7); (4) release while the escrow was still Open and before its deadline reverted `ReservationNotReleasable` (0xd74a1795); (5) WORKER-CODE settled the escrow and the DEPLOYER — a stranger to that escrow, proving the release is genuinely permissionless — released it (tx 0xb298782687a13b43fa1ac9f75b5e3234e22b812bd15fea9f10a1f9dad4d163ea), restoring headroom to exactly 24,000; (6) a second release reverted `ReservationAlreadyReleased` (0xbc361360). Every one of these is a real on-chain result, not a Foundry-only check.

priorRedeployment.reason: Grade (series — frontier/commodity) added as a discriminant across ClaimType/tokenIdFor/RateAttestation, enforced by both mint (series must match) and settleWindowClose (series AND printDate — the claim's own default day — must both match). Design review found grade completely unmodeled: nothing tied a claim or its rate attestation to a specific Touchstone Assay print series, so a frontier claim could previously have defaulted against a blended or commodity rate, and within the ±50% settlement band a caller could settle against a stale, more favourable print. See docs/gate-market-spec.md §4.3/§4.4 (corrected the same commit) and RateAttestationVerifier.sol/WorkClaim.sol's own doc comments for the full account. Covered by 4 new unit tests (series-mismatch-at-mint, series-mismatch-at-settle, printDate-mismatch-at-settle, tokenIdFor differs across series) plus the invariant handler now fuzzing both series values — full suite 137/137 (contracts) and 217/217 (gate-market-agents) before redeploying.
priorRedeployment.whyTheWholeTrioMovedNotJustWorkClaim: Same structural reason as the 2026-09-26 redeployment below: CapacityBond's constructor takes WorkClaim's own address as an immutable, precomputed via vm.computeCreateAddress before WorkClaim exists (DeployGateMarket.s.sol); ClaimRouter is pinned to CapacityBond the same way. All three redeployed together as one script run.

priorRedeployment.liveSmokeTest: Before resuming P5: a real mint_claim (ORCHESTRATOR, 10 mSIU code-class, genuinely publisher-signed SERIES_COMMODITY attestation) succeeded on-chain (tx 0x5df5c83b940651c81f029eacd78e5cead81b5bbd5ff9fd9a144c390674916599, block 47376230) — confirms the new bytecode's series check accepts a genuinely matching attestation, not just that it compiles. A second attempt with the identical claim (declared SERIES_COMMODITY) but an attestation genuinely signed for SERIES_FRONTIER reverted exactly as designed: `SeriesMismatch(0x6a33dd97c27182e82445945d5176f9e8f757598cf3cdc2b0d74eee7238b4c63b, 0x28b9bd511509601dd60a2359acd77ace0051da8b8fd3a5d60e5ce73794ae0f82)` (frontier attested, commodity expected) — a real on-chain revert, not a Foundry-only check. SERIES_FRONTIER()/SERIES_COMMODITY() also read back on-chain and confirmed to match packages/gate-market-agents/src/chain/rate-attestation.ts's own SERIES_FRONTIER/SERIES_COMMODITY constants exactly, independently computed (viem keccak256) versus the deployed contract's own public constants — same cross-implementation discipline as rate-attestation-cross-implementation.test.ts.

priorRedeployment.reason: serveRedemption had no window-closed check: a routed issuer could race settleWindowClose with a late passed=true report after the window closed and escape a genuine default. Fixed in WorkClaim.sol (WindowClosed() revert once block.timestamp >= ct.windowTo, mirroring the same guard already on presentForRedemption), covered by two new unit tests and a new invariant (invariant_noServeSucceededAfterWindowClosed, confirmed at FOUNDRY_INVARIANT_RUNS=10000 — 640000 calls, 0 reverts across all 6 invariants) before redeploying.
priorRedeployment.whyTheWholeTrioMovedNotJustWorkClaim: CapacityBond's constructor takes WorkClaim's own address as an immutable, precomputed via vm.computeCreateAddress before WorkClaim exists (DeployGateMarket.s.sol) — the two are mutually address-pinned at construction, so WorkClaim cannot be redeployed in isolation; ClaimRouter is pinned to CapacityBond the same way. All three redeployed together as one script run.

WorkClaim.notes: escrow_ is the TouchstoneEscrow already deployed on this chain (data/deployments/base-sepolia.json, 2026-08-18) — the same one packages/gate-market-agents already pays through. WorkClaim only reads it. This bytecode carries everything the prior trio did (settlement-rate band, rate-attestation binding, serveRedemption window guard, the series/printDate discriminant) plus reserveForWork/releaseReservation. Its ABI now exposes nine state-mutating functions rather than seven; NoAdminPath.t.sol asserts that exact set, so the growth was a reviewed change rather than a silent one.

capacityLots.note: Bonded live, 2026-09-28, immediately after the fourth deploy — real testnet USDC, real transactions, both classes (code/extract) per issuer. Deliberately smaller than every prior trio's: see redeployment.scarcitySizing above for why the old sizing could not bind. issuanceLimit = committedCapacityHours * measuredRateMilliSiuPerHour * 0.5 (CapacityBond.ISSUANCE_RATIO_BPS); bondedUsdc plays no part in it. classId = keccak256(bytes("code")) / keccak256(bytes("extract")), unchanged by the redeploy since a classId depends only on the class string.
capacityLots.rateFiguresAreFixtures: Neither committedCapacityHours nor measuredRateMilliSiuPerHour is a measurement, here or in any prior trio — the earlier 1000h x 120,000/80,000 mSIU per hour were illustrative too. These were chosen so the issuance limits land on 24,000 and 16,000 mSIU while preserving the deliberate 3:2 inequality between the two issuers that spec §3.5 calls for. Stated plainly rather than presented as a throughput result.
capacityLots.priorTrioSizing: Every trio before 2026-09-28: 1000 committed hours, 120,000 (ISSUER-A) / 80,000 (ISSUER-B) mSIU per hour, 10 USDC bonded per class, giving 60,000,000 / 40,000,000 mSIU limits.

history.reason: P4 showed every authoring run finishing in one turn regardless of model — a capable ORCHESTRATOR has no reason to subcontract, so P5 window 1 could never show emergent delegation with gpt-5.1 still assigned. Reassigned to a weaker, cheaper, non-frontier model per the user's own stated preference (make delegation rational, not scripted), verified empirically first rather than assumed.

empiricalVerification.finding: Failed to solo the same P4-style gate-authoring job cleanly. Two real, distinct signals, both disclosed rather than only citing the parse failure: (1) the raw response was prose-wrapped with markdown fences plus a separate trailing friction JSON block, breaking the simple first-brace/last-brace parser; (2) its own attempted gate source contained a genuine bug (execSync called with an argv-array second argument — execSync takes a command string plus options, not argv like execFile/spawn). Together: real evidence of lower capability, not just a formatting quirk.
empiricalVerification.outcome: Used as the real ORCHESTRATOR model per the plan's own decision rule (fails/struggles solo -> use it, delegation is rational).

history.reason: The weak-model window (data/gate-market/runs/p5-window1-2026-09-26T07-06-28-003Z/) showed a second, more severe failure mode: on its second real turn (context now including its own first failed attempt), mistral-small-3.2-24b-instruct produced no parseable tool-call JSON at all and was removed from the run before ever facing a delegation/asset-choice decision. A weak enough model to guarantee it can't solo the job is also too weak to reliably coordinate at all — the two properties don't separate cleanly for this model. User's own correction: pair a capable model with a structural constraint instead (information asymmetry — see docs/gate-market-spec.md's own §8.3 vs the ORCHESTRATOR-specific job description in packages/gate-market-agents/src/cli/p5-window1-full-run.ts, which now withholds the technical contract/reference materials from ORCHESTRATOR's own prompt entirely, so it cannot author regardless of model capability). Multi-hop/delegation is now a required, disclosed structural property of this window, not an emergent one — but F1's own question (which asset an agent pays in when it has a real, unbiased choice) was never about whether delegation happens, so it stays a genuine, unscripted measurement.

mainnetRequirements: Same as packages/contracts/README.md's own Gate Market mainnet preconditions: split the publisher key (print-signing vs rate-attestation-signing) before any real deployment, and the CapacityBond-goes-to-a-new-chain precondition (the daily print-publish automation must anchor to that chain's own TouchstoneAttestation first).
